description: Regression suite for SentinelPH's Level 1 (legitimate/grey_area/malicious) + Level 2 (9-subtype) SMS scam classifier. Combines known past failures, adversarial official-vs-spoofed domain pairs, must-never-flag OTPs, and baseline coverage across all 9 subtypes. Examples flagged must_not_flip:true are locked regression checks: any future model or heuristic change that flips their prediction should fail CI. Subtypes wrong_number_baiting, impersonation_family, political_campaign, and charity_appeal were dropped from scope on 2026-09-27 because the training data contains no real examples of these patterns; their remaining examples are retained with must_not_flip:false as documentation of the gap, pending future data collection.

changelog.change: Scoped from 13 to 9 subtypes. Downgraded must_not_flip to false for examples of wrong_number_baiting, impersonation_family, political_campaign, and charity_appeal.

examples.text: PHLPOST - The package has arrived at the warehouse. Please confirm your address at https://phpost.life/ (Please reply 1 to activate the link)
examples.note: Original false negative that triggered the Level 2 rebuild; phpost.life is not a PHLPOST-owned domain and must always be caught as phishing regardless of model updates.

examples.text: PHLPOST: Your parcel with tracking number RA123456789PH has arrived at the Quezon City Sorting Center. Track your delivery at https://phlpost.gov.ph/track
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_001 - identical scenario and brand, but on the real phlpost.gov.ph domain. Confirms the model keys off domain legitimacy, not brand mention alone.

examples.text: Your GCash Authentication Code is 839102. Do not share this code with anyone.
examples.note: Canonical legit OTP format - no link, no callback, explicit non-share instruction. Must never be flagged malicious or the product becomes unusable for everyday logins.

examples.text: BPI Alert: Your account has been locked due to suspicious activity. Verify immediately at bpi-secure-update-ph.com
examples.note: bpi-secure-update-ph.com is a lookalike domain, not bpi.com.ph. Mislabeling this as a legitimate bank_activity_alert was a known audit gap.

examples.text: Hey Mark, are we still meeting for golf this Saturday?
examples.note: SCOPE-DROPPED: wrong_number_baiting is out of scope as of 2026-09-27. Retained with must_not_flip:false to track the gap. Re-add to scope when training data is collected.

examples.text: Get P500 Cashback on Shopee 6.6 w/ BDO Credit Cards on Jun 5-7! Enroll your Promo ID 432A4649AA.
examples.note: Real co-branded bank-retailer promo with a promo ID instead of a link; tests that promo IDs and cashback language don't get over-triggered as phishing just because a bank is named.

examples.text: BDO reminds you: we will NEVER ask for your OTP, PIN, or password through SMS, call, or email. Report suspicious messages to report@bdo.com.ph.
examples.note: One of three BDO anti-scam PSAs mislabeled malicious in the last audit - likely due to alarming keywords (OTP, password) despite being a defensive warning, not a request.

examples.text: BDO Fraud Alert: If you receive a text or call asking you to click a link or share your One-Time PIN, do not respond. Hang up and call our official hotline (8631-8000).
examples.note: Second mislabeled BDO PSA - heuristic rules flagged 'click a link' and 'One-Time PIN' phrasing even though the message instructs the user not to comply.

examples.text: Paalala mula sa BDO: Hindi kami nangangailangan ng iyong OTP o password sa pamamagitan ng text o tawag. I-report ang kahina-hinalang mensahe sa aming official channels.
examples.note: Third mislabeled BDO PSA, Filipino-language version - confirms the fix generalizes across English and Tagalog phrasing of the same anti-scam warning.

examples.text: BDO: Your account has been temporarily suspended due to suspicious activity. Verify now at bdo-secure-update-ph.com to avoid permanent lock.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_027 - same bank and 'suspicious activity' framing, but on a spoofed domain instead of bdo.com.ph.

examples.text: Lazada: Congrats! You've been selected to claim a free gift. Claim here: lazada-rewards.vip/claim
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_035 - same brand and reward framing as the legitimate voucher promo, but on an unofficial .vip domain.

examples.text: J&T Express: Your parcel could not be delivered due to incomplete address. Update your details now: jt-express-ph.click/update
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_024 - identical courier and delivery-failure premise, but jt-express-ph.click is not J&T's registered domain.

examples.text: GCash: You have a pending cash-in of PHP 25,000.00. Verify your MPIN to receive it: gcash-verify.net/claim
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_028 - mimics GCash's real cash-in notification format, but legitimate GCash never asks users to submit their MPIN via an external link.

examples.text: Shopee: Your account has unusual login activity and will be suspended in 24 hours. Confirm your identity: shopee-account-verify.top
examples.note: Suspicious .top TLD paired with account-suspension urgency - a core brand-impersonation + suspicious-TLD pattern the heuristic rules are meant to catch.

examples.text: Maya: Your wallet has been temporarily locked for security reasons. Unlock it here: maya-secure.xyz/unlock
examples.note: Suspicious .xyz TLD impersonating Maya; included alongside reg_014 to confirm the pattern generalizes across e-wallet brands, not just one.

examples.text: DSWD: Your Ayuda cash assistance of PHP 3,000 is ready for release. Claim now: dswd-ayuda.xyz/claim
examples.note: Government-relief impersonation targeting a real social program (DSWD Ayuda); tests generalization beyond bank/courier brands to government agencies.

examples.text: SSS/Pag-IBIG: Your salary loan of PHP 15,000 has been approved. Complete your release by verifying your info here: sss-pagibig-release.life
examples.note: Combines two real government agencies into one lure and uses a .life TLD, echoing the phpost.life pattern from reg_001 in a different brand context.

examples.text: NTC: Your SIM will be permanently deactivated for failure to register. Register immediately at ntc-simregister.xyz to avoid disconnection.
examples.note: Exploits the real SIM Registration Act requirement - a high-relevance PH-specific lure that heuristics must catch via domain, not by recognizing the topic as fake.

examples.text: PLDT: Your monthly bill is overdue. Settle immediately to avoid disconnection: pldt-billing.top
examples.note: Utility-bill impersonation with a suspicious .top domain; rounds out phishing_link coverage across telco/utility brands.

examples.text: J&T Express: Your parcel 623000198234PH is out for delivery today. Rider: Ronnie, 09181234567.
examples.note: Routine courier update with a named rider and real-format tracking number, no link at all - baseline low-risk delivery example.

examples.text: LBC: Your shipment is now at LBC Sucat Hub and will arrive within 1-2 business days. Track at lbcexpress.com.
examples.note: Official LBC domain and standard shipment-status language; part of the general delivery_tracking baseline set.

examples.text: Lazada: Your order #LZD90213 has been delivered. Salamat sa pamimili sa Lazada!
examples.note: Post-delivery confirmation with no link or CTA - should never be confused with the reward-claim phishing variant in reg_011.

examples.text: Shopee: Your package is out for delivery and will arrive today. Track your order in the Shopee app.
examples.note: In-app tracking directive instead of an external link, a common legitimate courier pattern worth covering explicitly.

examples.text: J&T Express: Your parcel 623000123456PH is out for delivery today. Track it at jtexpress.ph/track.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_012 - identical delivery scenario, but the link resolves to J&T's real jtexpress.ph domain.

examples.text: Ninja Van: Your parcel has been picked up and is on its way to the sorting facility. ETA: 2 days.
examples.note: Covers a courier brand outside the GCash/BDO/PHLPOST cluster to check the model isn't overfit to a small brand list.

examples.text: 2GO: Your cargo booking #2GO55231 has departed Manila and is expected to arrive in Cebu on Sep 30.
examples.note: Inter-island cargo tracking, a less common but realistic PH courier scenario for delivery_tracking diversity.

examples.text: BDO: You have sent PHP 2,500.00 to Juan D. via BDO Pay&Go on Sep 27. Manage your account at bdo.com.ph. Ref# 004821.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_010 - same bank and 'account' framing, but a routine transaction notice on the real bdo.com.ph domain instead of a suspension threat.

examples.text: GCash: You've successfully cashed in PHP 2,000.00 via 7-Eleven. Check your balance in the app or at gcash.com.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_013. Downgraded from must_not_flip:true on 2026-09-27 during scope-down — reg_027 (BDO adversarial pair) retains the hard-block role for this subtype since BDO has historically produced more audit issues.

examples.text: BPI Alert: A withdrawal of PHP 5,000.00 was made from your account ending in 1234 at BPI Cubao ATM.
examples.note: Standard ATM withdrawal notice with masked account digits and no link - baseline legitimate alert format.

examples.text: Maya: Your cash-in of PHP 1,000.00 via GCash padala was successful. New balance: PHP 4,320.00.
examples.note: Cross-wallet transfer confirmation; tests that inter-wallet transaction language doesn't get flagged just for naming two e-wallet brands in one message.

examples.text: Metrobank: A purchase of PHP 899.00 was made using your debit card at SM Supermarket. If not you, call our hotline immediately.
examples.note: Includes a security callout ('if not you, call') without a link - checks the model doesn't treat any fraud-warning phrasing as inherently malicious.

examples.text: Shopee: 9.9 Mega Sale starts now! Up to 90% off + Free Shipping. Shop now sa Shopee app.
examples.note: Flagship annual sale event promo with hyperbolic discount language but no external link - baseline brand_marketing example.

examples.text: Globe: Enjoy GOMO's Php 99 unli data promo! Reply STOP to opt out of promos.

examples.text: Jollibee: Bagong Chickenjoy Bucket Treat available na sa lahat ng branch. Order via Jollibee app!

examples.text: Lazada: Your 9.9 Super Show voucher is ready! Claim it now at lazada.com.ph/vouchers before it expires.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_011 - same claim-your-gift framing, but on Lazada's real lazada.com.ph domain, confirming domain-based discrimination rather than keyword-based.

examples.text: Zalora: Take an extra 20% off sale items this weekend only. Shop the sale on the Zalora app.

examples.text: LTO: You have an unsettled traffic violation of PHP 2,500. Pay within 24 hours at lto-payment.info to avoid warrant of arrest.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_088 - same agency (LTO), but a fabricated fine with a threat of arrest and an unofficial .info domain instead of a routine renewal reminder.

examples.text: NLEX/SLEX: Your RFID account has insufficient balance and an outstanding toll of PHP 350. Settle now: nlex-toll.top
examples.note: Toll-road RFID scams are a recurring, high-volume PH pattern; must always be caught given how routine legitimate RFID top-up reminders otherwise are.

examples.text: BIR: Notice of tax delinquency. Failure to settle within 3 days will result in asset freeze. Call 0917-XXX-XXXX now.
examples.note: Callback-based (no link) fine scam impersonating a tax authority; confirms urgent_fine_toll detection isn't solely dependent on a URL being present.

examples.text: Meralco: Your electric bill is overdue. Your service will be disconnected today unless you settle via this link: meralco-bills.icu
examples.note: Utility disconnection threat with same-day urgency, a high-pressure variant using a suspicious .icu TLD.

examples.text: LTFRB: Your ride-hailing driver's account has a pending violation of PHP 1,000. Settle immediately to avoid suspension.
examples.note: Targets gig-economy drivers specifically, a narrower but realistic PH audience segment for this subtype.

examples.text: MMDA: You have an unpaid traffic citation. Pay online now to avoid your license being flagged: mmda-citation.top
examples.note: Traffic-citation variant distinct from the LTO pair, broadening coverage across different PH traffic authorities.

examples.text: NBI: There is a pending warrant of arrest under your name. Call this number immediately to clear your record: 0917-XXX-XXXX.
examples.note: Fear-based law-enforcement impersonation with no financial figure stated upfront, testing detection without an explicit peso amount.

examples.text: SSS: You have an unpaid contribution penalty of PHP 1,200. Settle today to avoid loan disqualification: sss-penalty.xyz
examples.note: Government-benefits penalty framing, rounding out urgent_fine_toll coverage across a fourth PH agency.

examples.text: Congratulations! Your number won PHP 50,000 in the GCash Anniversary Raffle. Claim: gcash-promo2026.com
examples.note: Unsolicited-win framing tied to a real e-wallet brand anniversary, a very common PH scam template.

examples.text: SM Malls 25th Anniversary: You are our lucky winner of a brand new iPhone! Reply YES to claim.
examples.note: Reply-based claim mechanism instead of a link, showing the subtype isn't defined by URL presence.

examples.text: PCSO: Your mobile number won 2nd prize sa 6/42 lotto promo. Text your full name and address to claim.
examples.note: Impersonates the actual government lottery agency (PCSO), which never notifies winners by unsolicited SMS - a high-priority must-catch pattern given the agency's real public trust.

examples.text: Shopee: You've been randomly selected in our Lucky Draw! Claim your PHP 10,000 GCash prize now, reply CLAIM.
examples.note: Cross-brand prize scam pairing Shopee's name with a GCash payout, a common cross-brand lure structure.

examples.text: Nescafe: Congratulations, you are our monthly raffle winner of PHP 20,000! Claim your prize by replying with your full name and address.
examples.note: FMCG/consumer-brand raffle impersonation, adding brand diversity beyond finance/telco/e-commerce.

examples.text: Globe/Smart: You have won a free load prize of PHP 500! Claim now by texting CLAIM to this number.
examples.note: Small prize amount designed to feel plausible and low-stakes, testing that prize size doesn't reduce classification confidence.

examples.text: Manalo ng PHP 100,000! I-claim ang iyong premyo bilang aming paraan ng pagbibigay pabalik sa komunidad. Text CLAIM ngayon.
examples.note: Charity-flavored language wrapped around a cash-prize claim; tests the reward-vs-cause decision rule against charity_appeal.

examples.text: Good day! I am Mr. John Williams from the UK National Lottery Board. You have inherited GBP 850,000. Contact us to process your claim.
examples.note: Classic foreign-lottery/inheritance scam template, included to check generalization beyond PH-branded prize scams.

examples.text: Kamusta na, matagal na tayong hindi nag-usap. Kumusta trabaho mo dyan sa Dubai?
examples.note: OFW-context catch-up message, a very common legitimate PH texting pattern given the large overseas worker population.

examples.text: Salamat sa tulong mo kanina ha, lifesaver ka talaga.
examples.note: Short gratitude message with no request at all - tests that the model doesn't need an explicit topic to classify low-risk personal texts correctly.

examples.text: Pre, may dala ka bang extra charger? Nawala yung sakin.
examples.note: Casual favor-ask between friends involving a lost item, superficially similar in structure to scam openers but with no money or credentials involved.

examples.text: Happy anniversary sa inyo ni Marga! God bless sa inyong pamilya.
examples.note: Celebratory greeting text, a common and entirely benign SMS category that should never trigger any risk signal.

examples.text: Nasaan ka na? Nasa gate 3 na ako ng mall.
examples.note: Real-time meetup coordination text, representative of high-frequency everyday personal messaging.

examples.text: Miss na kita Mama, kumusta dyan sa probinsya? Ingat lagi.
examples.note: Family check-in message that must not be confused with the impersonation_family subtype simply because it names a family member - no money ask is present.

examples.text: Sorry, mali ata number, pero okay ka lang? Gusto lang makapagkwentuhan, medyo lonely lang ngayon.
examples.note: Deliberately ambiguous wrong-number opener with zero scam hook. Previously must_not_flip:true as a boundary case for wrong_number_baiting — downgraded on 2026-09-27 when that subtype was dropped from scope.

examples.text: BPI: 391045 is your One-Time PIN for your online banking login. Huwag ibahagi sa kahit kanino.
examples.note: Bilingual OTP format combining an English code with a Tagalog non-share warning; must never be flagged given how central OTP delivery is to core banking flows.

examples.text: Maya: Use code 738201 to verify your device. This code expires in 3 minutes.
examples.note: Device-verification variant of an OTP (rather than login or transaction), broadening two_factor_auth coverage across use cases.

examples.text: Shopee: Your verification code is 552091. For your security, do not share this code with anyone, including Shopee staff.
examples.note: E-commerce login OTP; confirms coverage extends beyond banking and e-wallet brands to marketplace logins.

examples.text: Lazada: 604738 is your verification code. Valid for 5 minutes. Do not share this with anyone.
examples.note: Near-duplicate structure to reg_079 from a different marketplace brand, testing consistency of OTP handling across similar templates.

examples.text: BDO: Your enrollment verification code is 219034. This code is confidential and should not be shared.
examples.note: Account-enrollment OTP rather than a login or transaction code, rounding out the OTP lifecycle stages covered.

examples.text: Maya: 847210 is your code to confirm your fund transfer of PHP 5,000.00. Do not share this code.
examples.note: Transaction-confirmation OTP that includes a peso amount, checking the model doesn't over-weight monetary figures inside an otherwise standard OTP.

examples.text: GCash: 305914 is your verification code to link a new device to your account. Ignore this message if you did not request it.
examples.note: Includes an explicit 'ignore if not requested' instruction, a legitimate-OTP marker distinct from phishing's typical 'act now' urgency.

examples.text: Reminder: Your dental appointment sa Metro Dental Ortigas ay bukas, Sept 28, 2PM. Reply C to confirm.
examples.note: Standard clinic reminder with a simple reply-to-confirm mechanism, a baseline appointment_reminder example.

examples.text: PhilHealth: Your appointment for member data update is on Oct 3, 9AM, PhilHealth Alabang branch.
examples.note: Government-agency appointment notice with no fine, threat, or link - contrasts directly with the malicious government-impersonation examples elsewhere in the suite.

examples.text: Your appointment with Dr. Santos (Makati Medical Center) is confirmed for Mon, 10AM. Text CANCEL to reschedule.
examples.note: Private hospital scheduling confirmation, a common legitimate healthcare SMS pattern.

examples.text: Paalala: Bakuna ng inyong anak sa Barangay Health Center ay sa Oct 5, 8AM-12NN. Dalhin ang immunization card.
examples.note: Public health/vaccination reminder at the barangay level, representative of grassroots government SMS communication.

examples.text: LTO: This is a reminder that your driver's license renewal is due on Oct 15. Renew online at lto.gov.ph or visit any LTO office.
examples.note: Adversarial pair partner to reg_046 - same agency (LTO), but a routine renewal reminder on the real lto.gov.ph domain instead of a fabricated fine with a threat of arrest.

examples.text: DFA: Your passport appointment is confirmed for Oct 20, 8:00 AM, DFA NCR East. Bring your appointment confirmation and requirements.
